points.description: The bridge table maps destination MAC addresses (stations) to outgoing LAN interfaces.
The bridge table starts out empty.
During backward learning, when a frame arrives with source address Q on LAN L, the bridge adds an entry stating that Q can be reached over L.
Each learned table entry is timestamped, and the timestamp is used to update or purge old entries.
When the destination address of a frame is in the table, the bridge forwards the frame only on the associated interface (selective forwarding) instead of flooding it.
A benefit of this selective forwarding is that it reduces unnecessary flooding, duplication, congestion and wasted bandwidth compared with flooding.
